citation_hygiene.rule: Every path, T/W number, policy name and git ref named in this file must exist. This is no longer a convention a human has to remember — `go run ./cmd/doclint .` checks it, and CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .`.
citation_hygiene.why_this_block_still_exists: It records what the check is FOR. Two consecutive passes cited 'Global Constraint 9, constraints.md' — a file that never existed in any branch — and the citation was what justified deferring a task that, when finally checked on its merits, cost one optional field and one wiring line. The rule that citation stood in for: a pass closes its own queue item and does not widen into neighbouring modules; where the correct shape does require changing another package, that is recorded in Deviations with an argument — it is not grounds to defer the task silently.
citation_hygiene.exceptions_list: docs/not-yet-written.md — the single list doclint reads. It goes red in BOTH directions: a line that has become unnecessary is a finding too, so the list cannot rot into a dumping ground.

closed_this_pass.what: IPv6 blocking under ipv6_block (queue item 1; SPEC §6.9). T28 written and green in netns
closed_this_pass.head: ca7a096
closed_this_pass.decision_log: implementation-notes.md, section 'Этап 8 — блокировка IPv6 (`ipv6_block`, T28, W48)' — six measurements, the mechanism, the policy border, four Deviations
measured_not_assumed: With the tunnel up, IPv6 leaves through the PHYSICAL interface and the connection to an outside peer establishes. The tunnel table is empty for IPv6 and never participates in the lookup, because Up only ever ran `ip route add` — an IPv4-family command. So the leak goes PAST the TUN, and the !ok branch of netstack parsing has nothing to do with it: a packet that never reaches the device is a packet the stack never sees.

unreachable → ENETUNREACH, prohibit → EACCES, blackhole → EINVAL. unreachable chosen: blackhole is silence, which §5.6 forbids, and ENETUNREACH is the signal Happy Eyeballs falls back to IPv4 on without delay.
sysctl disable_ipv6 was rejected BY MEASUREMENT: it destroys global addresses and does not bring them back, so the snapshot diverges by three lines — the mechanism breaks §8.4 by construction.
The netstate snapshot did not see IPv6 rules at all (`ip -o rule show` is IPv4-only). A rules6 section was added; verified by the reverse experiment — Reclaim without its -6 half drops T29.
closed_this_pass.spec_correction: SPEC §6.9 said IPv6 'is blocked at the level of TUN routes'. Measurement disproved it; the section is rewritten. This is the project's standing rule at work: the measurement wins, the spec is edited.
closed_this_pass.policy_border: ipv6_block switches exactly one step of Up: `ip -6 rule add unreachable priority 32000`, installed FIRST and therefore removed LAST (the journal unwinds LIFO), so there is no moment where the tunnel is up and IPv6 is open. Not switched: rules6 in netstate (§8.4 contract) and the -6 half of Reclaim (a startup obligation, §6.2) — neither branches behavior, so neither could go red.
closed_this_pass.registry: docs/verification-agent.md §5.8 row W48 (TestW48UpBlocksIPv6, privilege-free: the list of Up steps is a pure function, upSteps) and §6 flag row ipv6_block. T28 lives in internal/l3 and is NOT named in the policy registry, by the standing rule: negcheck runs `go test`, and L3 skips without HOP_L3, so it would be green under any state of the flag — exactly the fixture_bad shape.

closed_this_pass.what: doclint — a document's claim about state must rest on something executable (the parallel task; not part of plan_order)
closed_this_pass.head: 09af0d2
closed_this_pass.decision_log: implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое', including where the recognition boundary was drawn and why
closed_this_pass.shape: internal/doclint (logic) + cmd/doclint (thin wrapper, like negcheck). Four checks: a T*/W* number must exist as a Go test (the number in the Test* function name or in its doc comment); a policy name must be registered in internal/policy; a path must exist; a branch or commit named in HANDOFF.json must resolve in git (-git=false switches that half off, and CI uses it: a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history).
closed_this_pass.recognition_boundary: Deliberately conservative — a linter that shouts at every other word gets switched off. Paths are read only out of backticks (in JSON, out of string values) and only when the first segment is an existing top-level entry: one condition drops every quotation from refs/ and every import. A bare filename WITH a line reference is not checked at all (that is how foreign code is cited; own code is cited by full path). .json is excluded from extensions — nodes.json/health.json live on the user's disk. A policy is recognised only as `name=` or as a table cell containing nothing else.
closed_this_pass.red_before_fixes: 34 findings, including all three known true positives (ipv6_block unregistered, T25-T28 missing, the stale branch block in this very file). Fixed by writing docs/not-yet-written.md where the absence is honest, and by correcting the document where the claim was simply false (PLAN.md pointed at this very file under a name it has never had; T31 existed but carried no number in its doc comment).
closed_this_pass.no_flag: A linter is not a product policy, and realtimelint carries none either. Argued explicitly in implementation-notes.md rather than left implicit.

parallel_passes_trap.what_happened: Two of the three passes independently took the next free registry number and both landed W48. Nothing catches this inside a single pass: each read the registry, saw W47 as the last row, and was right at the time it looked.
parallel_passes_trap.resolved_how: 0e1a198. W48 stayed with ipv6_block, whose tests carry the number in their NAMES (TestW48UpBlocksIPv6); the snapshot guard became W49 and got its number into the doc comment of TestStackStatsSeesRealBypassNAT — which doclint then demanded, because a registry number with no test behind it is exactly its first check.
parallel_passes_trap.rule_for_the_next_parallel_run: Before a parallel pass writes a registry row, the controller hands out the numbers — or every pass writes its number into the test itself, where the collision is a compile-time-visible fact rather than a merge surprise.

next_task.name: Refuse, don't silence, IPv6 connections that predate `up`
next_task.why_first: The one §5.6 hole the IPv6 pass measured and deliberately left open. After the rule lands, an ALREADY ESTABLISHED IPv6 socket leaks nothing but hangs to its own TCP timeout, and send() still reports success. On a dual-stack desktop that is every open browser connection at the moment of `up`. §5.6 says refuse, never go silent — and this is silence.
next_task.measured_starting_point: `ss --kill -6 -t dst [<addr>]` under `unshare -Urn` returns 0 and turns the connection into ECONNABORTED. CAP_NET_ADMIN is enough, no root. ss ships in the same iproute2 as ip, so no new dependency. It needs CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY, which is not universal — that is degradation, not breakage, and the pass must decide what happens without it.
next_task.shape_question: One sweep right after the rule is installed suffices, because after the rule no NEW IPv6 connection can be established. Whether to shell out to ss or to speak SOCK_DESTROY over netlink directly is the design call; the platform layer today only shells out to ip.
next_task.flag: its own, e.g. ipv6_kill_established. NOT ipv6_block: with ipv6_block=off no rule exists, so no socket would ever be stale and the guard would go red for the wrong cause. Same argument that kept bypass_rebind out of bypass_sink.
next_task.test_gap: An L3 test that opens an IPv6 connection BEFORE `up` and asserts it is refused, not hung, after. The stand is already built: internal/l3/harness_test.go grew a veth peer with a TCP echo server on fd00:9:9::2 and waitAddrsSettled for this pass.

repo_hygiene_finding.what: Two compiled binaries, hop and hopd, are tracked in git (~48 MB each). They predate all of these passes — the last commit touching them is ba4459c.
repo_hygiene_finding.why_it_matters_here: They are also a source of false matches for any tool that greps the tree: doclint skips them only because it reads named documents, and a registry grep for a number hits the binaries' string tables.
repo_hygiene_finding.not_done: Removing them rewrites nothing but the index, yet it is a repository decision, not a pass decision. Left for the human.

notes.doclint: New this pass. Fast. Runs in CI as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 40 policies as of this pass, ~20-35 min wall clock on this machine — this is expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. Per-task gate only needs the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name>; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: Build once, run under an unprivileged user namespace: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). This works without root — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the fresh netns. Reusing the built binary across repeated unshare invocations is much faster than `go test` per run.
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). `go run ./cmd/realtimelint .` is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. `gofmt -l ./internal` reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code.
notes.flake: internal/l2 TestT10SlowNodeKeepsConnectionAlive occasionally flakes on timing under load; re-run it alone before recording it as a regression.
